- [FACT] User has been experimenting with weathering techniques on model builds.
- [FACT] User completed a 1/700 scale USS Arizona battleship model in about two weeks.
- [PREFERENCE] User wants to improve their weathering techniques for model builds.
- [PREFERENCE] User is particularly interested in achieving a realistic rust effect on the hull of their models.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Weathering typically appears as reddish-brown streaks, patches, or blooms on the surface of a ship's hull.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended materials for rust effects include acrylic paints (rust colors: burnt sienna, rust, iron oxide, or Vallejo's Rust & Chipping Medium), weathering pigments, and a small brush.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested techniques for rust effects include applying a base coat, creating rust streaks, applying rust blooms, using weathering pigments, salt weathering, chipping, masking tape streaks, and blending.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised to experiment with different rust colors and shades, and to apply rust effects in thin layers.
